headline: Approved order conditions for five projects, including 9 Dalton Street and 20 and 22 Goldthwaite Road; postponed six hearings to September 14.
summary: The commission issued or amended order conditions for five projects, including the Malden Woods subdivision and a City vegetation project at Indian Lake Dam. It also issued several certificates of compliance, lifted or ratified enforcement orders, and approved its FY26 Annual Report. Six public hearings were postponed to 09/14/2026.
decisions: Postponed public hearings for six items, including 35 State Road and 99 Sears Island Drive, to 09/14/2026 and extended the constructive grant deadline to 10/06/2026, 3-0.
Issued a negative determination of applicability for 4 Spring Valley Road (CC-2026-057), 3-0.
Issued order conditions for 149 West Boylston Drive (CC-2026-056), 3-0.
Issued amended order conditions for 0 Whippoorwill Drive and 0 Danielle's Way (Malden Woods Subdivision), 3-0.
Chose not to require a liner for the infiltration unit at 9 Dalton Street.
Issued order conditions for 9 Dalton Street (CC-2026-048), 3-0.
Issued order conditions for 46, 51, and 52 Modoc Street (CC-2026-054), 3-0.
Issued order conditions for 20 and 22 Goldthwaite Road (CC-2026-060), 3-0.
Issued a Certificate of Compliance for 222 Brook Street (CC-2019-009), 3-0.
Issued a partial Certificate of Compliance for 74 and 76 Valmor Street (CC-2023-075), 3-0.
Issued a Certificate of Compliance for 1195 Grafton Street (CC-2025-046 & DEP#349-1421), 3-0.
Approved the project change request for Elm Park Playground (CC-2025-002), 3-0.
Lifted an enforcement order for incomplete wetland replication tied to the Westside Veterinary Clinic, 3-0.
Lifted an enforcement order for unpermitted disturbance within 100 feet of a catch basin (address not named in the minutes), 3-0.
Issued an enforcement order for 88 Webster Street (CC-2023-025 & DEP#349-1361) to carry out a restoration plan, 3-0.
Ratified the enforcement order for 11 Holden Street (CC-EO-2026-003), 3-0.
Ratified the enforcement order for 142 Olean Street (CC-EO-2026-004), 3-0.

Conservation Commission 
Meeting Minutes 
August 24th, 2026 
City Hall – Levi Lincoln Chamber,  
with remote participation options available via Zoom online at 
https://worcesterma.zoomgov.com/j/1604682366 and  
call-in number 1-669-254-5252 (Meeting ID: 160 468 2366). 
 
Attendance: 
Commissioners 
Present: 
 
 
Commissioners 
Absent:  
 
Staff Present: 
Devin Canton, Vice Chair 
Lindsay Nystrom, Commissioner 
Stuart Kirshner, Commissioner  
 
Diane Fratoni, Chair 
 
Eric Flint, Division of Planning & Regulatory Services (DPRS) 
Mattie VandenBoom, Division of Planning & Regulatory Services 
(DPRS)  
Call to Order 
Commissioner Canton, acting as Chair in the absence of Commissioner Fratoni, called the 
meeting to order at approximately 5:30 PM. 
Requests for Continuances, Postponements and Withdrawals 
Item 1 – Providence and Worcester Railroad ROW – Request for 
Determination of Applicability (CC-2026-033) 
Request to postpone the public hearing to 09/14/2026 & extend the constructive grant 
deadline to 10/06/2026 
 
Item 3 – 35 State Road (MBL 32-019-00316) – Notice of Intent (CC-2026-045 
& DEP#349- 14xx) 
Request to postpone the public hearing to 09/14/2026 & extend the constructive grant 
deadline to 10/06/2026 
 
Item 7 – 99 Sears Island Drive – Notice of Intent (CC-2026-052 & DEP#349-
14xx) 
Request to postpone the public hearing to 09/14/2026 & extend the constructive grant 
deadline to 10/06/2026
Item 9 – 3 Mann Street (MBL 14-033-00002) – Notice of Intent (CC-2026-058 
& DEP#349-14xx) 
Request to postpone the public hearing to 09/14/2026 & extend the constructive grant 
deadline to 10/06/2026 
 
Item 10 – 300 & 301 Barber Avenue (MBL 22-015-00001 & 22-015-00002) – 
Notice of Intent (CC-2026-059 & DEP#349-14xx) 
Request to postpone the public hearing to 09/14/2026 & extend the constructive grant 
deadline to 10/06/2026 
 
Item 12 – 278 Grove Street, 4 Brookfield Street, 4 & 4A Powers Court – Notice 
of Intent (CC-2026-061 & DEP#349-14xx) 
Request to postpone the public hearing to 09/14/2026 & extend the constructive grant 
deadline to 10/06/2026  
 
Upon a motion by Commissioner Nystrom, seconded by Commissioner Kirshner, the 
Commission voted 3-0 to postpone the public hearings as discussed.  
New Business – Request for Determination of Applicability 
2) 4 Spring Valley Road (MBL  55-017-00201) – CC-2026-057 
Neil Hassett, the applicant, explained that the project involved reconstructing an existing 
deck that had collapsed over the winter. The new deck would retain the exact footprint of 
the previous structure, with upgrades including pressure-treated framing and deck boards, 
updated railings, and newly dug code-compliant footings.  
 
Ms. VandenBoom reported that the project initially appeared in the building permit 
system, where staff flagged it because of the wetland buffer. She reported no concerns with 
the project.     
 
Commissioner Canton asked about the old footings.  Mr. Hassett explained the old, 
outdated supports will be removed.      
 
Upon a motion by Commissioner Nystrom, seconded by Commissioner Kirshner, the 
Commission voted 3-0 to issue a negative determination of applicability as discussed.    
List of Exhibits:  
Exhibit A: Request for Determination of Applicability; dated 07/22/2026; prepared 
by Neil Hassett    
Old Business – Notice of Intent  
4) 149 West Boylston Drive (MBL 13-035-0001A) - CC-2026-056 & DEP# 349-
1457 
Gregory LaCroix and Dave Presch, Pare Corporation, on behalf of the applicant, City of 
Worcester Department of Sustainability and Resilience, presented updates on the City’s 
vegetation management project along the crest of Indian Lake Dam. They explained that 
since the previous hearing, they had received and responded to comments from both staff 
and MassDEP. The most significant change involved adjusting the Bordering Land Subject 
to Flooding (BLSF) elevation from 542 to 542.4 feet, increasing the mapped flood coverage
area. The team also addressed Commission concerns about how vegetation behind a chain-
link fence would be maintained, explaining that handheld tools such as weed whackers 
would be used due to limited equipment access. Questions about material stockpiling 
triggered the addition of a designated stockpile area located as far from resource areas as 
possible. 
 
Mr. Flint reported only minor comments after completing a full review and expressed no 
concern about the updated plans.   
 
No comments from the public or staff.   
Upon a motion by Commissioner Nystrom, seconded by Commissioner Kirshner, the 
Commission voted 3-0 to close the public hearing.  
Mr. Flint noted the work is approved as a limited project pursuant to 310 CMR 10.53(3)(i).   
In addition to the standard conditions, Mr. Flint recommended special conditions for 
wetland flagging, maintenance of flood storage capacity, native seed mix application to 
disturbed areas, wood removal, dust controls, dewatering, equipment placement, and spill 
prevention.        
Upon a motion by Commissioner Nystrom, seconded by Commissioner Kirshner, the 
Commission voted 3-0 to issue the order conditions as discussed.    
List of Exhibits:  
Exhibit A: Notice of Intent; dated 07/20/2026; prepared by George LaCroix, Pare 
Corporation   
Exhibit B: Site Plan; dated 07/17/2026; prepared by Allen R. Orsi, Pare Corporation 
Exhibit C: Department of Environmental Protection Comments; dated 08/10/2026; 
prepared by Rebecca Gendreau  
Exhibit D: Division of Planning & Regulatory Comments; dated 08/17/2026; 
prepared by Eric Flint & Mattie VandenBoom 
Exhibit E: Response to Comments; dated 08/24/2026; prepared by George LaCroix 
& David Pretsch, Pare Corporation  
 
Old Business – Request Amended Order of Conditions  
5) 0 Whippoorwill Drive & 0 Danielle’s Way (aka Malden Woods Subdivision) 
(MBL 32-011-0001A & B through -0007A & B; -00008 through -00013; -
0014A & B; & -0015A & B); the Whippoorwill Drive Right-of-Way; and the 
westerly portion of the Castine Street Right-of-Way 
Nikita Shugrue and Alex Wood, Thompson Liston Associates representing Whippoor LLC, 
the applicant, presented revised plans. They explained that the Commission had 
previously objected to patios and a driveway encroaching into the 30‑foot buffer. In 
response, the applicant reconfigured plans so all patios, now impermeable, and the 
driveway for Lot 10A are fully outside the buffer. They also introduced the possibility that 
the developer might install decks instead of patios for certain lots during construction. To 
streamline future approvals, they requested an amendment allowing decks if they also
remained outside the 30‑foot buffer and maintained equal or lesser impervious area.   
Mr. Flint supported incorporating this flexibility directly into the Order of Conditions and 
advised including limitations based on zoning setbacks, which prohibit decks in some side-
yard areas.  
Commissioner Kirshner asked what materials would be used for the deck.  Mr. Wood 
confirmed the decks would be made from wood.   
No comments from the public.   
Upon a motion by Commissioner Nystrom, seconded by Commissioner Kirshner, the 
Commission voted 3-0 to close the public hearing.  
Mr. Flint noted the work is approved as a limited project pursuant to 310 CMR 10.53(3)(i).   
Mr. Flint recommended modifications to the existing Order of Conditions including 
allowing the applicant to construct decks or patios and adjusting condition 34 related to 
sequencing.        
Upon a motion by Commissioner Nystrom, seconded by Commissioner Kirshner, the 
Commission voted 3-0 to issue the amended order conditions as discussed.   
List of Exhibits:  
Exhibit A: Request for Amended Order of Conditions; dated 07/14/2026; prepared 
by Patrick Healey, Thompson Liston Associates    
Exhibit B: Site Plan; dated 07/10/2026; revised 08/07/2026; prepared by Patrick 
Healey, Thompson Liston Associates  
 
New Business – Notice of Intent 
6) 9 Dalton Street (MBL 34-019-00002) – CC-2026-048 
Kevin Quinn, Quinn Engineering on behalf of the applicant, Amanda Russo-Folco, described 
the construction of a five‑unit multifamily building. He explained how stormwater would be 
collected in catch basins, treated in a stormwater treatment unit, and discharged to a 
chamber gallery designed to retain runoff until the system reaches a specified capacity.   
 
Mr. Flint explained staff’s biggest concern relates to groundwater proximity to the 
underground chambers of the infiltration unit.  He asked if there is a risk for groundwater to 
seep into the infiltration unit and enter the city’s drainage system.  Mr. Quinn that the 
seasonal high groundwater remained below the chamber bottom, negating risk of 
groundwater infiltration.   
 
Mr. Quinn explained that a liner could be installed in infiltration unit but was not necessary 
and might reduce beneficial groundwater recharge.   
 
After a brief discussion, the Commission chose not to require a liner for the infiltration unit.
No comments from the public.   
Upon a motion by Commissioner Nystrom, seconded by Commissioner Kirshner, the 
Commission voted 3-0 to close the public hearing.  
Mr. Flint noted the work is approved as a limited project pursuant to 310 CMR 10.53(3)(i).   
In addition to the standard conditions, Mr. Flint recommended special conditions 
stormwater management system maintenance, infiltration unit inspection, certification of 
stormwater infrastructure, wood removal, dust controls, dewatering, cement truck 
washing, and sand and salt.  He recommended ongoing conditions for stormwater 
management system maintenance, and sand and salt.    
Upon a motion by Commissioner Nystrom, seconded by Commissioner Kirshner, the 
Commission voted 3-0 to issue the order conditions as discussed. 
 
List of Exhibits:  
Exhibit A: Notice of Intent; dated 07/07/2026; prepared by Chris Keenan, Quinn 
Engineering   
Exhibit B: Site Plan; dated 06/22/2026; revised 08/07/2026; prepared by Kevin J. 
Quinn, Quinn Engineering  
Exhibit C: Stormwater Report; dated 06/18/2026; prepared by Kevin J. Quinn, 
Quinn Engineering  
Exhibit D: Division of Planning & Regulatory Comments; dated 07/29/2026; 
prepared by Eric Flint & Mattie VandenBoom  
Exhibit E: Response to Comments; dated 08/07/2026; prepared by Chris Keenan, 
Quinn Engineering  
 
6) 46, 51, & 52 Modoc Street (MBL 38-017-1A-11, 38-017-1A-10, & 38-017-1A-09) 
- CC-2026-054 
Attorney Donald O’Neil, joined by engineer Joseph Graham, presented a revised 
subdivision layout involving ten total dwelling units formed by five semi-detached 
structures. The project required a new Notice of Intent because the original 2018 approval 
expired before construction of these remaining lots.  Mr. O’Neil explained that each unit 
would include an individual infiltration chamber to manage stormwater.  
 
Mr. Flint explained that staff reviewed updated plans and a revised stormwater report, 
noting that their previous concerns related to perimeter controls, planting plans, and 
stormwater calculations had been resolved.  
 
Commissioner Canton asked about the project phasing.  Mr. O’Neil explained the road has 
already been constructed.  Mr. Flint noted through aerial imagery that the lots already 
appeared to be cleared and some foundation excavation had begun.   
Upon a motion by Commissioner Nystrom, seconded by Commissioner Kirshner, the 
Commission voted 3-0 to close the public hearing.
In addition to the standard conditions, Mr. Flint recommended special conditions 
Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan, stormwater management system maintenance, 
infiltration unit inspection, certification of stormwater infrastructure, dust controls, 
dewatering, cement truck washing, construction monitoring reports, sand and salt, 
wetland permitting.  He recommended ongoing conditions for stormwater management 
system maintenance, and sand and salt.      
Upon a motion by Commissioner Nystrom, seconded by Commissioner Kirshner, the 
Commission voted 3-0 to issue the order conditions as discussed.  
List of Exhibits:  
Exhibit A: Notice of Intent; dated 07/15/2026; prepared by Donald J. O’Neil, Esq.   
Exhibit B: Site Plan; dated 07/02/2026; revised 08/20/2026; prepared by Joseph 
Graham  
Exhibit C: Stormwater Report; dated 04/26/2026; revised 08/20/2026; prepared 
by Joseph Graham    
Exhibit D: Division of Planning & Regulatory Comments; dated 07/22/2026; 
prepared by Eric Flint & Mattie VandenBoom  
Exhibit E: Response to Comments; dated 08/20/2026; prepared by Joseph Graham  
 
11)  20 & 22 Goldthwaite Road (MBL 39-021-00045 & 39-021-43+44) - CC-2026-
060 
Nikita Shugrue and Alex Wood, Thompson Liston Associates on behalf of the applicant, 
Pappas Prime Properties, LLC Whippoor LLC, the applicant, presented a redevelopment 
project involving demolition of an existing single-family house and construction of a new 
28‑unit multifamily apartment building while retaining the existing three‑family structure 
at number 20 Goldthwaite Road.  Although no wetland buffers exist on-site, the filing was 
required due to proximity to municipal catch basins.  
Ms. VandenBoom confirmed that a previously flagged area potentially subject to isolated 
flooding did not qualify as a regulated resource after further study. The only staff comment 
concerned the landscape plan, which needed greater inclusion of native trees and shrubs.  
Commissioner Canton and Commissioner asked for clarification on the snow storage areas 
and parking configuration.  Mr. Shugrue clarified that interior garage parking is proposed 
supplemented the external parking count and that a special permit process for reduced 
parking was underway through the Planning Board.      
No comments from the public.   
Upon a motion by Commissioner Kirshne, seconded by Commissioner Nystrom, the 
Commission voted 3-0 to close the public hearing.  
In addition to the standard conditions, Ms. VandenBoom recommended revised plans 
including at least 50 percent native tree and shrub species, stormwater management 
system maintenance, infiltration unit inspection, certification of stormwater
infrastructure, dust controls, dewatering, cement truck washing, sand and salt.  She 
recommended ongoing conditions for stormwater management system maintenance and 
sand and salt.      
Upon a motion by Commissioner Nystrom, seconded by Commissioner Kirshner, the 
Commission voted 3-0 to issue the order conditions as discussed.   
List of Exhibits:  
Exhibit A: Notice of Intent; dated 08/05/2026; prepared by Nikita Shugrue, 
Thompson Liston Associates    
Exhibit B: Site Plan; dated 07/24/2026; prepared by Patrick Healey, Thompson 
Liston Associates 
Exhibit C: Stormwater Report; dated 06/03/2026; prepared by Patrick Healey, 
Thompson Liston Associates 
Exhibit D: Division of Planning & Regulatory Comments; dated 08/18/2026; 
prepared by Eric Flint & Mattie VandenBoom  
 
Other Business 
13)   Request for Certificate of Compliance 
a. 222 Brook Street (CC-2019-009) 
Ms. VandenBoom reviewed the Certificate of Compliance request for 222 Brook Street.  
The project involved construction of a low-rise apartment building.  She noted that an as-
built plan and engineer’s letter confirmed the project was constructed as approved. The 
site was inspected on August 18 and found the entire property, including a steep hillside, 
fully stabilized with healthy plantings. 
 Upon a motion by Commissioner Kirshner, seconded by Commissioner Nystrom, the 
Commission voted 3-0 to issue the Certificate of Compliance. 
List of Exhibits: 
Exhibit A: Certificate of Compliance Request; dated 07/07/2026; prepared by Tom 
Corbett, Zero Point Development, Inc.  
b. 74 & 76 Valmor Street (CC-2023-075)  
Ms. VandenBoom explained that a partial Certificate of Compliance was being requested 
for a duplex.   She confirmed the site was fully stabilized and noted that previously flagged 
dead tree plantings had been replaced. 
Upon a motion by Commissioner Kirshner, seconded by Commissioner Nystrom, the 
Commission voted 3-0 to issue a partial Certificate of Compliance. 
List of Exhibits: 
Exhibit A: Certificate of Compliance Request; dated 07/02/2026; prepared by JAE 
Wor, LLC
c. 1195 Grafton Street (CC-2025-046 & DEP#349-1421)  
Ms. VandenBoom explained this project involved directional drilling to replace utility 
lines.  She explained that staff conducted a site visit on August 18th and confirmed the site 
was fully stabilized.   
 
Upon a motion by Commissioner Kirshner, seconded by Commissioner Nystrom, the 
Commission voted 3-0 to issue a certificate of compliance.   
List of Exhibits: 
Exhibit A: Certificate of Compliance Request; dated 07/09/2026; prepared by Sam 
Keffestan, BSC Group    
14) Project Change Request  
a. Elm Park Playground (CC-2025-002) 
Mr. Flint reviewed a project change request from the Parks Department for Elm Park. The 
Parks Department previously received a negative determination for playground 
resurfacing and now sought approval to replace pads under 21 picnic tables. Given the 
minor nature of the work and proposed erosion controls, staff recommended processing it 
as a project change under the existing DOA. 
Upon a motion by Commissioner Nystrom, seconded by Commissioner Kirshner, the 
Commission voted 3-0 to approve the project change request.  
15) Enforcement Order and Violation Updates 
a. 133 Lake Avenue North (CC-2020-007) 
b. 99 Wildwood Avenue (CC-EO-2020-009) 
c. 269 James Street (CC-EO-2021-007) 
d. 4 Tiffany Avenue (CC-EO-2023-001) 
e. 570 Lincoln Street (CC-EO-2023-010) 
f. 198 Granite Street (CC-EO-2024-001) 
g. 86 Webster Street (CC-EO-2024-003) 
h. Salisbury Hill (CC-EO-2024-005 & DEP#349-1253) 
i. 262 Mill Street (CC-EO-2024-007) 
Ms. VandenBoom reviewed the history of the Enforcement Order.  The enforcement order 
was issued in 2024 for incomplete wetland replication required back in 2001 when the 
Westside Veterinary Clinic was constructed.  The replication area has since been 
completed and monitored for two growing seasons.  A final report confirms native 
vegetation and a functional wetland (>75% wetland plantings).   
 
Upon a motion by Commissioner Kirshner, seconded by Commissioner Nystrom, the 
Commission voted 3-0 to lift the Enforcement Order.
j. 142-158 Wildwood Avenue (CC-EO-2024-010) 
k. 1256 West Boylston Street (CC-EO-2025-001) 
l. 13 Holden Street (CC-EO-2025-002 & DEP# 349-1409) 
m. 270 Webster Street (CC-EO-2025-004) 
n. 34 Eskow Road & 224 Southwest Cutoff (CC-EO-2025-006) 
o. 148A Tory Fort Lane (CC-EO-2025-007, CC-2023-016, & DEP# 349-1356) 
p. 1259 West Boylston Street (CC-EO-2025-008) 
q. 145 Newton Ave North (CC-EO-2025-009) 
Ms. VandenBoom explained that unpermitted disturbance within 100 feet of a catch basin 
previously triggered an enforcement order.  The homeowner was required to stabilize the 
site and allow staff to inspect the site during 2026 growing season.  A staff inspection 
confirmed full stabilization of the site.     
 
Upon a motion by Commissioner Kirshner, seconded by Commissioner Nystrom, the 
Commission voted 3-0 to lift the Enforcement Order.  
 
r. 757 Salisbury Street (CC-EO-2025-010 & CC-2023-005) 
s. 9 & 13 Elton Street (CC-EO-2025-011, CC-2024-083, & DEP#349-1407) 
t. 612 Grove Street (CC-EO-2026-001) 
u. 342 (aka 344, 346, & 348) Lake Avenue (CC-EO-2026-002 & DEP#349-1435) 
v. 88 Webster Street (CC-2023-025 & DEP#349-1361) 
Nick Facendola, Level Design Group, LLC, reviewed the proposed restoration plan from 
wetland scientist Matt Marro.  The restoration plan involves the removal of riprap, 
regrading, soil decompaction, topsoil addition, and native replanting.  
 
Mr. Flint recommended the Commission issue an enforcement order to implement the 
restoration plan.  
 
Upon a motion by Commissioner Kirshner, seconded by Commissioner Nystrom, the 
Commission voted 3-0 to issue the Enforcement Order as discussed.  
 
w. 11 Holden Street (CC-EO-2026-003) 
Ms. VandenBoom explained that an unpermitted covered porch was constructed within 
the 30‑foot buffer to Delany Brook. Staff issued an enforcement order requiring an as-built 
plan to be provided. 
 
Upon a motion by Commissioner Nystrom, seconded by Commissioner Kirshner, the 
Commission voted 3-0 to ratify the Enforcement Order.  
 
x. 142 Olean Street (CC-EO-2026-004) 
Mr. Flint stated that vegetation removal and installation of an above-ground pool directly
adjacent to the shoreline prompted an enforcement order. The homeowner was 
cooperative and explained that some shrubs were damaged by a fallen tree, leading to 
cleanup and unintended over-removal. Staff required retention of a wetland scientist to 
develop a restoration plan, likely to include native plantings and consideration of 
relocating the pool outside the buffer. 
 
Upon a motion by Commissioner Kirshner, seconded by Commissioner Nystrom, the 
Commission voted 3-0 to ratify the Enforcement Order.  
 
There was no discussion of item 15a-15h, 15j-15p & 15r-15u.  
 
16)   Open Space Discussion 
 There was no discussion of item 16.   
 
17)   Discussion of Active Projects 
There was no discussion of item 17.   
 
18)   Communications 
There was no discussion of item 18. 
19)   Approval of Minutes – August 13th, 2026 
Upon a motion by Commissioner Nystrom, seconded by Commissioner Kirshner, the 
Commission voted 3-0 to approve the minutes.   
20)   Update to Wetlands Protection Ordinance and Regulations  
Mr. Flint provided an update on ongoing revisions to the Wetlands Protection Ordinance, 
particularly on simplifying administrative approvals, which will be presented in redline 
form at a future meeting. 
   
21)   Approval of FY26 Annual Report 
Mr. Flint reviewed the draft Fiscal Year 26 Annual Report detailing permitting activity, 
land management, and open space accomplishments by the Conservation Commission.  
 
Upon a motion by Commissioner Nystrom, seconded by Commissioner Kirshner, the 
Commission voted 3-0 to approve FY26 Annual Report. 
   
22)    Commission Liaison Update 
Liaison updates for Lake Commission and Community Preservation were brief, with no 
significant new information. 
 
23)   Policies and Procedures 
There was no discussion of item 23. 
Adjournment:  
Upon a motion by Commissioner Kirshner, seconded by Commissioner Nystrom, the 
Commission voted to adjourn at approximately 6:25 PM.
